# Independent audit: facet moments and shared simplex volumes



## Exact fixed-mass facet moments

Source: `candidate 6ac02348e3ceb9a9`.

For 0<t<|F|, proper cap quantiles are unique in every nonconstant
in-plane direction and vary continuously. The two dominated-convergence
arguments correctly use null intrinsic cutting hyperplanes. Compactness
of the cap-centroid image and the proved finite Caratheodory reduction
make its convex hull compact. The signed threshold comparison proves
that this hull is exactly the moment body of fractional selectors of
mass t. Thus compactness is proved without an unjustified weak-* limit.

The threshold dual infimum attains the support value at the actual
volume-t cap threshold. Flat ambient directions and the full-mass
case are separate. Uniqueness of a nonflat maximizing density follows
from the strict sign away from a null hyperplane. The claimed relative
interior, strict convexity, and boundary-moment consequences then follow
from the compact support-gap and separation arguments given.

Substitution in the actual one-sided derivative has the correct
coefficient (2t+s)y in the prescribed nonnormalized moment. Separation
of the proved compact moment body gives a genuine equivalence to the
full family of first-order inequalities, not to global criticality.
The normal-direction affine constraint is checked and flat directions
are included. Full-facet saturation and equal-section-volume rigidity
are conditional as stated.

For planar fibers, the extremal fixed-mass interval means are exactly
the centers of its two extreme length-t subintervals. Combining this
moment interval with the ACTUAL middle section inclusion cancels the
unknown support-facet length. The bound
|y-c_K|/s <= rho(1-rho)/(1+2rho) is correct, as are its exact square
identity and the endpoint-distance ratio1/sqrt(3). No cap-area depth
bound follows from that chord constraint alone, and none is asserted.

## Shared enclosing simplex geometry

Source: `candidate f5833eb86e30876b`.

For an interior point p of B, the larger pyramids from p to the simplex
facets partition the simplex up to null boundaries. The actual smaller
facet pyramids are inside B and have relative volumes f_i lambda_i(p).
Approximating a boundary p from int B justifies the stated all-point
inequality. No assumption that B contains the simplex centroid is used.

In the planar refinement, the convex hull of the three actual edge
intervals has precisely the three possible corner gaps. Their normalized
areas are products of the two incident endpoint gaps. Increasing gaps
only relaxes the bound; the resulting separately affine box polynomial
has its maximum at a box vertex. Its eight values give the largest
product of two edge gap budgets. A single corner truncation attains the
result for prescribed lower bounds, with the third edge retained fully.
Sharpness is not falsely claimed for three independently prescribed
EXACT intersection lengths or for genuine critical configurations.

Facet-capacity substitution is legitimate only for proper opposite
endpoint cuts. The compared parallel sections have the same affine
Jacobian, so their ratios survive a continuous affine change. This is
an actual common-body constraint; it supplies no mixed cap-mass lower
bound or assertion that B is the whole enclosing simplex.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
